column1: # Dataset: Business Survivability Scores by Neighborhood - Tampa Bay (2026)
# Description: Predicted probability (0-100%) that a business type survives 2+ years at neighborhood level in Tampa Bay
# Scores are based on 100+ location factors and 570
column2: 000+ real business outcomes across 24 US metros

column1: # Citation block: publisher=StreetSpring; dataset_name=StreetSpring Survivability Datasets 2026; dataset_version=2026.10.05; dataset_doi=10.5281/zenodo.22287996 (concept DOI
column2: always the newest version); as_of_date=2026-10-05; license=CC-BY-4.0

column1: # source_url: empty in every row. held for this release: it resolves for only about a third of rows until the place pages are built. An empty column is honest; a third-filled one is not.
# source_url_business_type: absolute and verified against the live site on 2026-10-02; filled on 58.2% of rows. Empty means the page was not proven to exist
# Ranking: rows are ranked on p90_survivability_score
column2: the score at a good address (90th percentile of the scored locations inside the place)
column3: NOT on the average. Ranking a place by its average ranks how uniform it is
column4: not how good its best locations are.

column1: # Place kinds: city neighbourhoods and whole municipalities are ranked in SEPARATE lists. place_kind says which. A rank is only ever against places of the same kind
column2: and total_ranked_neighborhoods_for_business_subtype is the size of that kind's list
column3: which can be fewer than ten.

column1: # Not every place is ranked: a place needs at least 10 scored locations of its own and at least 5 peer places of the same kind. Unranked places keep their score and their page; the rank
column2: tier and list-size columns are empty for them.

column1: # Not every business type is ranked: the rank
column2: tier and overall columns cover the business types StreetSpring publishes guides for. The other scored types keep their scores with empty rank columns.

column1: # Overall rank: neighborhood_overall_rank ranks the place against places of the same kind on neighborhood_overall_score
column2: the mean p90_survivability_score of its ranked business types; ties break on the mean average
column3: then scored locations. The four neighborhood_overall_* scores are means over the same ranked rows.

column1: # Scale: projected chance of lasting two or more years
column3: calibrated per sector; never the model's raw output

column1: # Note: This file carries one row per business type and place. Its score is the projected chance of lasting two or more years
column2: averaged across the price points StreetSpring scores separately in the tool (most types have 5). The 146 business types here are base types; the tool offers 500+ business types
column3: counting each type at each of its price points.

column1: # Business types: StreetSpring scores 500+ business types: 153 base business types
column2: most of them at 5 price points
column3: which is 569 type-and-price combinations you can choose in the tool.

column1: # Columns: city = Metro slug (for example philadelphia).; neighborhood = Neighborhood slug inside the metro; the row's place.; business_subtype = Business type slug (for example italian-restaurant); the row's business. The file's own count is in the README and on its page.; business_type_lookup = Display name of the business type (for example Italian Restaurant).; avg_survivability_score = The projected chance
column3: that this business type lasts two or more years at a typical address in this neighborhood. The rankings use p90_survivability_score
column4: the good-address score.; max_survivability_score = Best address in the neighborhood for this business type
column5: 0 to 100.; the rest are in the README

column2: Where should I open a given business in this metro? Filter business_subtype to the type and place_kind to neighborhood (or town)
column3: sort by neighborhood_rank_for_business_subtype ascending. The ranking is on p90_survivability_score
column4: the chance of lasting two or more years at a good address; avg_survivability_score is the typical address.

column2: What should I open in a given neighborhood? Filter neighborhood to the place
column3: sort by business_subtype_rank_for_neighborhood ascending: the top rows are the business types most likely to last there.

column2: How do two neighborhoods compare for the same business? Filter business_subtype to the type and neighborhood to the two places (same place_kind); compare p90_survivability_score for the best-address view and avg_survivability_score for the typical address.
Which neighborhoods are strongest overall? Filter place_kind to neighborhood
column4: sort by neighborhood_overall_rank ascending. neighborhood_overall_score is the mean p90 of the place's ranked business types.
